note: Same 4-step fp16 rollout, init 2026-04-05T00, GPU3, run once per configuration. Read timings are all taken under .venv312, because that is the runtime the backend is moving to. No application code was changed: the third configuration patches _zarr_encoding from scripts/profile_blosc3.py.

zarr2 lz4-5 shuffle.codec: Blosc(lz4, clevel=5, shuffle) - today's default, read from the store's own .zarray

zarr3 zstd-0 noshuffle.codec: ZstdCodec(level=0) - what zarr 3 picks when nobody says otherwise

forward_s_per_step.verdict: 2.66 s/step everywhere; Python 3.12, numpy 2.4 and the new torch build are neutral on the GPU

write_s_per_step.verdict: the 2.6x penalty splits: ~0.43 s is zstd instead of lz4, ~0.22 s is zarr 3's own write path at the same codec

read_s_blosc_threads_4.caveat: blosc thread count does nothing for the zstd store - that codec is zarr's own, not blosc. Its threads=4 row moving at all is variance.

decision: keep Blosc lz4-5 shuffle and set it explicitly on migration. The zarr 3 default buys 1.39 GB per ten-day run and costs 17 s of write per run and ~40% on every regional read, which is the wrong side of a trade for a backend whose job is fast analysis.

codecs_on_one_real_forecast_step.note: the same measurement bench_compress.py makes, but on Aurora's output instead of on ERA5

why_bench_compress_overstated_the_ratio: bench/results/compress.json measured 1.97 for lz4-5 shuffle, but on ERA5 fields. CDS packs ERA5 as int16 with a scale factor, so the decoded float32 sits on a uniform lattice: t at level 6 has 46310 distinct values in 1038240 points, minimum gap exactly 2^-10. After shuffle the low mantissa bytes of such data are nearly constant. Aurora's own output has no lattice (minimum gap 1.5e-05) and the same codec reaches only 1.46, matching the 1.47 the real store gets. Every per-run size estimate derived from bench_compress is optimistic by about a third; the 7.3 GB/run in scripts/check_registry.py was right. Note also that shuffle helps ERA5 and hurts Aurora output: on the forecast, zstd-3 noshuffle (1.89) beats zstd-3 shuffle (1.55).
